title: Model-Based Normal Tissue Complication Probability Comparison Between Proton and Photon Therapies for Brain Tumors Complying With Planning Study Guidelines

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Model-Based Normal Tissue Complication Probability Comparison Between Proton and Photon Therapies for Brain Tumors Complying With Planning Study Guidelines》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · para0007】Proton beam therapy (PBT) lowers radiation doses to normal tissues surrounding tumors compared with photon therapy, potentially reducing adverse events, particularly within the complex and delicate structures of the central nervous system (CNS). However, PBT insurance coverage in Japan remains limited because of high costs and few available facilities. In addition, the necessity for prolonged posttreatment follow-up to observe late CNS toxicities, combined with substantial associated costs and rapid technological innovations, severely limits the implementation of randomized controlled trials. The significant costs associated with the extended follow-up make it difficult to conduct studies, and new innovations are likely to render study results of little use.

【Background · para0008】Normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) is a mathematical model based on the relationship between the prescription dose and adverse events for patients treated with radiation therapy. Langendijk et al1 defined the model-based approach as an attempt to verify the superiority of different treatments by comparing them with NTCP. This approach can show the usefulness of particle therapy for diseases where its benefits have been difficult to verify.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:

【Study design and patients · para0012】Eligible patients who initiated PBT between May 1, 2016, and April 30, 2021, at 13 participating institutions were registered in the Proton-net database and treated under a unified policy without expressing refusal to participate. Details on the policy are given in the supplementary material A.

【Patient characteristics · para0026】Table 2 contains characteristics of 66 patients. Of all patients, 59 (89.4%) had a diagnosis confirmed by histopathology, whereas the others had a clinical diagnosis. The histologic type of tumor was based on the 2016 edition of the CNS WHO classification because the patients were treated until 2021. The histologic types were glioblastoma (21 patients), glioma (17 patients), and meningioma (28 patients). There were no significant differences in CTV volume (P = .3863) or number of occupied areas (P = .4551) between the subgroups by histologic type.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:

【Results · para0025】The RATING score was 96%, and the score sheet showing the results is attached as a supplementary file.

【Conclusions · para0046】This study used multiple NTCP models in accordance with RATING and suggested that PBT was associated with lower NTCPs for selected endpoints compared with IMRT. PBT appears to be advantageous in sparing contralateral organs and structures for which low-dose exposure is clinically relevant. Furthermore, it shows the potential to reduce the risk of secondary cancer, especially in young patients and in disease groups with long expected survival. To further substantiate the benefits of PBT, NTCP models based on PBT-treated patients and external validation of existing models are needed.

【Figure 1 · fig0001】Figure 1 Benefit-tradeoff map comparing dosimetric outcomes of virtual IMRT and PBT. The plot displays median paired dose differences (IMRT −PBT) for key OARs, with error bars representing IQR. Points to the right of the red dashed line (difference >0) indicate lower metrics with PBT (favoring PBT); points to the left (difference <0) indicate lower metrics with virtual IMRT (favoring IMRT). Because endpoints include both dose-based (Gy[RBE]) and volume-based (%) metrics, horizontal magnitudes should not be compared directly across different OARs. This summarizes the direction and distribution of modality-related differences for each NTCP model input.Abbreviations: CTV = clinical target volume; gEUD = generalized equivalent uniform dose; IMRT = intensity modulated radiation therapy; NTCP = normal tissue complication probability; OAR = organs at risk; PBT = proton beam therapy; RBE = relative biological effectiveness.
